items.title: UK backs Somalia's path to security and political progress
items.description: The UK has reaffirmed its long-term commitment to Somalia during the first visit to the country by the minister for Development and Africa, Kirsty McNeill MP. items.titleIt: UK backs Somalia's path to security and political progress

items.description: (ANSA) - IL CAIRO, 25 AGO - The Italian Ambassador to Sudan, Silvio Mignano, presented his letters of credence today in Khartoum as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to the President of the Sudanese Transitional Sovereignty Council, Abdelfattah Al Burhan. items.titleIt: Italian Ambassador to Sudan Mignano Presents Credentials to Al Burhan

items.title: Ambassador Mignano on a mission to Sudan, the first Italian ambassador in Khartoum since 2023
items.description: (ANSA) - IL CAIRO, 25 AGO - The new ambassador to Sudan, Silvio Mignano—who had been based in Addis Ababa since the start of the conflict—carried out his first mission in the country. The mission included a stop in Port Sudan before moving on to Khartoum for the presentation of credentials. This was the embassy’s first mission to the capital since the evacuation in 2023. Italy is the first Western country to present its credentials. items.titleIt: Ambassador Mignano on a mission to Sudan, the first Italian ambassador in Khartoum since 2023

items.title: Somalia's New Speaker Got His Parliamentary Seat Through a Military Operation. His Career Was Built by Turkey.
items.description: That minister was Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur Jaamac — known in Somali political circles as Madaxa Na Furan. items.title: Somali Cabinet Approves Passport, Trade and Judicial Reforms
items.description: The council was briefed on Somalia's new third-generation electronic passport and was told that changes to personal data in issued passports have been stopped entirely to strengthen the document's credibility. Ministers also approved a Rules of Origin Bill allowing goods containing at least 30% Somali content to qualify for preferential treatment in regional markets. items.titleIt: Somali Cabinet Approves Passport, Trade and Judicial Reforms

items.title: Somalia Says 25 Al-Shabaab Militants Killed, Four Surrender
items.description: The Ministry of Defence announced the outcome in a press statement released on Saturday, describing the operation as part of the Federal Government of Somalia's ongoing military campaign against Al-Shabaab. items.titleIt: Somalia Says 25 Al-Shabaab Militants Killed, Four Surrender

items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.
items.titleIt: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab

Ambassador Diene expressed appreciation for Djibouti's longstanding contribution to peace and security in Somalia, including the continued deployment of Djiboutian troops under AUSSOM. items.title: Somalia Says 25 Al-Shabaab Militants Killed, Four Surrender
items.description: The Ministry of Defence announced the outcome in a press statement released on Saturday, describing the operation as part of the Federal Government of Somalia's ongoing military campaign against Al-Shabaab. According to the ministry, the strike targeted positions the group had established in Suullaay, an area where security forces have continued operations aimed at disrupting militant activity in central Somalia. items.title: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran
items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.
items.titleIt: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran

items.title: East Africa: From Red Sea to Sudan - Why Ethiopia's Instability Risks Destabilizing Horn of Africa
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The guns may not yet have returned to the scale seen during Ethiopia's devastating 2020-2022 war, but the warning signs are becoming impossible to ignore. Tigray is once again caught in a dangerous political and military confrontation, while the unresolved issues left behind by the Pretoria peace agreement continue to deepen.
items.titleIt: East Africa: From Red Sea to Sudan - Why Ethiopia's Instability Risks Destabilizing Horn of Africa

items.title: IPI: Africa Media Freedom Monitoring: April to June 2026
items.description: The International Press Institute (IPI) recorded nearly 100 cases of threats and attacks on journalists (82 male and 18 female) across 22 countries in sub-Saharan Africa between April and June 2026. Physical and verbal attacks, as well as arrests and detention, were the most frequent types of incidents. An Ethiopian journalist in exile was found dead in Kenya under suspicious circumstances.   Police and state security forces (55%) continued to be the primary perpetrators of attacks and threats against journalists, a trend that continues from the previous quarter. items.title: 5 teen far-right extremists cited in Arezzo
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, AUG 25 - Italian police on Tuesday cited five teenage far-right extremists for online radicalisation and using neo-Nazi and white supremacist slogans online in the south Tuscan city of Arezzo. The five, all minors, are accused of propaganda and incitement to crime based on racial, ethnic, and religious discrimination. They are being investigated by the Prosecutor's Office at the Juvenile Court of Florence following an investigation by the Arezzo Police.
